reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: serrated grain boundaries are known to impede dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding, and applying this to an FCC/BCC HEA coating at 650°C is a reasonable extension of established creep mechanisms.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with a well-defined control, measurable outcomes (creep rate, time-to-failure, strain distribution), and a decisive falsification criterion based on statistical significance.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is highly useful as it proposes a specific, microstructural modification (grain boundary serration) with a clear mechanism, directly addressing the research question on creep resistance in HEA coatings.
